chunk_findings.detail: `_families` computes `single=f in HOT_SINGLES`, but `resolve` accepts a declared `Command` whose `family` is a hot-single name with a non-empty `action`. The generated `Family` is then marked `single=True` even though its `members` map contains both the hot single’s empty action and the extra action. For example, with `ddflow_identify` in `TOOLS` and a command `ddflow_extra` declared as `family="ddflow_identify", action="extra"`, `_families` returns `Family("ddflow_identify", {"": "ddflow_identify", "extra": "ddflow_extra"}, single=True)`. A caller that sees `single=True` omits the action enum, making `extra` unreachable and breaking the hot-single invariant, while no error is raised.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/tools/families.py:135

chunk_findings.detail: The test passes `legacy={}`, so it never introduces a conflicting legacy mapping. A `resolve` implementation that prioritizes legacy entries whenever present would still pass this test because no legacy entry exists. The input `legacy={"ddflow_zed_go": ("ddflow_legacy", "old")}` is what would actually distinguish “declared wins” from “legacy wins”, and it is absent.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_declared_families.py:test_a_declared_family_and_action_win_over_the_legacy_placement

chunk_findings.detail: `fam.members` is a dict, so `len(set(fam.members)) == len(fam.members)` is tautologically true: dict keys are unique by construction, and duplicate action keys would already have been collapsed by assignment. For example, a generated members dict that assigns `"record"` twice silently overwrites the first value, and this test still sees one key and passes, so it cannot catch duplicate action generation.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_declared_families.py:test_actions_are_unique_within_a_family

chunk_findings.detail: The test checks `F.HOT_SINGLES` against a separate hardcoded tuple and then checks counts, but it never verifies that the families with `single=True` are exactly `F.HOT_SINGLES`. Swapping the `single=True` flag between `ddflow_gate` and `ddflow_brief` keeps `len(fams) == 15`, `len(F.FAMILIES) == 24`, and the `F.HOT_SINGLES` tuple comparison passing, so the property named in the test is not actually asserted.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_declared_families.py:test_nine_hot_singles_and_fifteen_families_make_24_tools

chunk_findings.detail: Adding `family` and `action` in the middle of the `Command` dataclass, before `reason` and the served-by/value fields, changes the positional meaning of every later field. In any environment where `Command` is constructed positionally — e.g. `Command("run self", False, {}, "debug parity", "self")` — the pre-change values for `reason` and the served-by field now bind to `family` and `action`, leaving `reason` and the later parity fields empty. This silently corrupts MCP parity decisions. These new fields should be appended at the end of the dataclass or the dataclass should be made keyword-only, unless all existing positional callers are updated.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/registry.py:590 (Command)

chunk_findings.detail: `resolve` does not reject every partially migrated `Command`. If a command has `action` set but `family` empty and its name exists in `_LEGACY`, the `elif family:` guard is false, so it falls through to `elif name in legacy:` and silently uses the legacy placement. For example, `DECLARED["ddflow_task_add"]` with `family=""` and `action="renamed"` returns legacy `Placement("ddflow_task", "add")` instead of raising. The declared `"renamed"` action is discarded, so `FAMILIES`/`ALIASES` can disagree with the declared matrix, violating the stated single-source rule.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/tools/families.py:resolve

chunk_findings.detail: The test claims a declared `Command.family`/`action` wins over the legacy placement, but it calls `F.resolve({"ddflow_zed_go": c}, legacy={})`. There is no conflicting legacy value, so the asserted precedence is never exercised. A `resolve` implementation that always prefers any non-empty legacy entry would still pass this test; it should pass something like `legacy={"ddflow_zed_go": ("ddflow_gate", "wrong")}`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_declared_families.py:test_a_declared_family_and_action_win_over_the_legacy_placement

chunk_findings.detail: The test checks that `F.HOT_SINGLES` equals the nine expected strings and that there are 15 non-single families, but it never checks that those nine hot-single names are present in `F.FAMILIES` (or `TOOLS`) as the `single` families. A faulty implementation could export the correct `HOT_SINGLES` tuple while omitting those tools from `F.FAMILIES` and `TOOLS`; all assertions in this file would still pass, leaving the required “9 hot singles” unverified.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_declared_families.py:test_nine_hot_singles_and_fifteen_families_make_24_tools

chunk_findings.detail: The added fields default to `""`, and the accompanying comment says an empty value falls back to the legacy placement table. This directly contradicts the change’s stated invariant that the declared-command matrix is the single source and that “import fails without one”: a new `Command` can be declared with no `family`/`action` and is explicitly allowed to defer to legacy mapping instead of being rejected. For example, `Command(name="foo", family="", action="")` is a valid declaration under this code, so a missing family/action does not fail import and the advertised tool set is not generated solely from the declared matrix.

chunk_findings.detail: `test_an_unplaced_tool_fails_import_time_resolution` does not actually exercise import-time resolution. It calls `F.resolve(...)` directly on a synthetic `Command`, so an implementation that defines `F.resolve` exactly as tested but never invokes it while `ddflow.surfaces.tools.families` is imported would still pass this suite even if the real declared matrix contains a command lacking `family`/`action`. The decision requires import to fail without one, so this test cannot catch the failure mode it is named for.

data.body:

In Server._m_tools_call, before _resolve_call, call family_schema.route(name, args): a str is an error result; a Routed replaces the name and args and its display name ('ddflow_gate action=record') is what _check_call reports, so 'missing required argument(s)' is prefixed with it. """MTD-family-route: `tools/call` of a family tool runs its member (the engine side of
MTD-family-schema's `family_schema.route`)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))
from conftest import run_cli

from ddflow.surfaces.mcp import Server


def _call(repo, tool, **args):
    reply = Server(repo).handle(
        {
            "jsonrpc": "2.0",
            "id": 1,
            "method": "tools/call",
            "params": {"name": tool, "arguments": args},
        }
    )
    result = reply["result"]
    return result["content"][0]["text"], bool(result.get("isError"))


@pytest.fixture
def inited(repo):
    run_cli(repo, "init")
    return repo


def test_a_family_call_runs_the_member_and_gives_the_flat_answer(inited):
    fam, fam_err = _call(inited, "ddflow_gate", action="list")
    flat, flat_err = _call(inited, "ddflow_gate_list")
    assert (fam, fam_err) == (flat, flat_err)
    assert not fam_err


def test_a_missing_required_argument_names_the_action(inited):
    text, err = _call(inited, "ddflow_gate", action="record")
    assert err
    assert "ddflow_gate action=record" in text
    assert "missing required argument(s)" in text


def test_an_argument_of_another_action_is_unknown_for_this_one(inited):
    text, err = _call(inited, "ddflow_gate", action="list", gate="critic", bogus="x")
    assert err
    assert "ddflow_gate action=list" in text
    assert "bogus" in text


def test_an_unknown_or_missing_action_is_an_error_naming_the_actions(inited):
    text, err = _call(inited, "ddflow_gate", action="frobnicate")
    assert err and "frobnicate" in text and "record" in text
    text, err = _call(inited, "ddflow_gate")
    assert err and "action" in text and "record" in text


def test_the_legacy_names_and_the_self_named_tools_still_answer_as_before(inited):
    text, err = _call(inited, "ddflow_doctor")
    assert not err
    text2, err2 = _call(inited, "ddflow_doctor", action="check")
    assert not err2
    assert text2 == text
    assert _call(inited, "ddflow_gate_list")[1] is False

chunk_findings.detail: `_description` builds the per-action required list with `_requires(t)`, which returns the member’s original property names. For a member whose own `action` argument is required (the file’s own `OP` comment lists queue, ci, prompts, hooks, export), the advertised description says `action`, but `family_entry`/`_union` rename that argument to `op` in the family schema and `route` maps `op` back to `action` later. Concrete case: `ddflow_admin` action `export` with an original required `action` yields `export(action)` in the description, while the only usable call shape is `{"action": "export", "op": "..."}`; `action` is already the family selector and no per-member `action` property exists. A caller that follows the description cannot satisfy that required argument and `_check_call` fails on the original missing `action`. The required list should rename the member’s `action` to `op`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/tools/family_schema.py:76

chunk_findings.detail: The suite never exercises a recognized family action with one of that member's required arguments omitted, e.g. `FS.route("ddflow_gate", {"action": "record"})` where `record` requires `id`. The intent explicitly requires "per-action required-parameter errors that name the action," but no test would fail if `_requires` dropped that rule, so this acceptance criterion is unverified.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_mcp_families.py::test_a_missing_action_names_the_actions

chunk_findings.detail: `_flat` imports the private helper `_schema` from `ddflow.surfaces.mcp`. The change's own context says `mcp.py` is leased for another task and its tools/call routing is moving to `MTD-family-route`; if that concurrent work moves or removes `_schema`, this import raises during test collection and fails this test even when `family_schema.family_listing()` and `route()` are correct.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_mcp_families.py::_flat

chunk_findings.detail: `_requires` returns raw property names from `TOOLS[tool]["properties"]` without re-mapping a member's own `action` to the family-facing `op` argument. For a family member such as the code's own comment names (`queue`, `ci`, `prompts`, `hooks`, `export`) whose underlying `action` argument is required, `_description` emits a bracket list like `ci(action)`. But `family_entry` exposes that member argument as `op`, and `route` expects `op` and maps it back to the member's `action`. A model that follows the description and supplies only `action=ci` (with no `op`) will be routed to the member with `rest={}` and then fail the member's required-argument check. The description should name the family argument `op`, not the original member property.
